premisesReverified.premise: 102 of 102 live fleet and patrol records fail their declared shape, and the guard refuses them with the faults named.
premisesReverified.verified: REPRODUCED, and then reproduced a second way. (a) In a harness: the branch's own recordShapeFaults over the live payloads (75 Samsara rows, 27 Spireon rows) refuses 102 of 102 with the same three fault kinds. (b) ON A DEPLOYED NON-PRODUCTION APP: https://app.smartcityos.io serving ea27024 answers status='refused', recordCount=0, refusalCount=75 and 27 on the two regions, with both lens chips at 0 roster rows painted. Neither lane nor harness is the only witness any more.

premisesReverified.premise: The three faults are three DIFFERENT kinds of thing, and collapsing them is the defect this operation keeps producing.
premisesReverified.verified: Each was decided from the payload and each landed on a different verdict: status = a TRANSLATION whose table is empty as a finding; operatorRef = THE DECLARED SHAPE IS WRONG AND THE DATA IS RIGHT; odometerBand = NEITHER OVER-DECLARED NOR MISSING UPSTREAM. The three are now handled by three different mechanisms (a declared translation table, a declared-absence clause, and a mapper that derives the value), which is the evidence that they were not collapsed.

premisesReverified.premise: Before synthesising an operatorRef, establish whether the vendor payload carries an operator identity AT ALL.
premisesReverified.verified: Read at source in smartcity-os, not inferred from the absence: server/routes/samsara.ts:1133-1137 says driver assignment is per-vehicle on this vendor and not bulk-fetchable in one call, so it is not included; server/routes/spireon.ts:182 builds the row with `officer: ""`. There is no identity to pseudonymise, so a reference would be a binding that was not resolved. The declared shape is wrong and the data is right.

premisesReverified.premise: odometerBand is either a missing upstream capability or a shape that over-declares.
premisesReverified.verified: Neither. The raw reading IS in the read: odometerMiles present on 72 of the 75 fleet rows, and the band is a bucket of that number. The mapping was simply never done. Kept required with NO declared-absence escape, so the 3 rows whose reading did not arrive are still refused and still say which field refused them.

premisesReverified.premise: Samsara's `unknown` is not a state: it is the absence of one, and mapping it onto the enum would be a fabricated value that reads as measured (the defect class ENFORCEMENT.md opens with).
premisesReverified.verified: Confirmed as the route's own fallback rather than a vendor word: the deployed d12-main-uat surface served `status: "unknown"` on 75 of 75 fleet rows, and Spireon's default is the same shape of fallback and visible at source (spireon.ts:177, `asset.status || "Unknown"`, which the same read served on 2 of 27 rows). Both are now refused as states and carried as declared absences.

premisesReverified.premise: A required field no source ever supplies must be decided from the payload before anything is declared.
premisesReverified.verified: Satisfied for all three fields; no field was declared away for convenience. The one field granted a declared-absence escape (operatorRef) is the one whose whole route cannot produce a value, and the escape is CONDITIONAL: it requires a non-empty basis string, only on feed records, and fixture records may never use it.

preRegisteredFalsifiers: F1 - 'The mapping was made by loosening the guard.' Violation: 102 of 102 raw live records are STILL refused after the change, with the same three faults; the two new guard clauses each produce a refusal the old clause could not express (a not-a-state token carried as a state; a bare null where a basis was required). Nothing added to recordShapeFaults lets an unchecked value through.

F2 - 'A live record asserting one of the four readiness bands was accepted.' Violation: LIVE_STATUS_TRANSLATIONS is declared and EMPTY for both kinds and the guard refuses a feed record asserting a band no row maps, by name. An empty table that is READ is a different object from an empty table that is decoration.

F3 - 'A missing reading was hidden by declaring the field absent.' Violation: odometerBand carries NO liveDeclaredAbsence, so the 3 fleet rows with no odometerMiles are refused rather than served with a blank, and the surface names the fault.

F4 - 'The declared absence became a blanket escape for any required field.' Violation: only operatorRef has one, and it is conditional (feed origin, non-empty basis string). A fixture record may never omit the field; a feed record with a bare null is refused. Four planted violations in src/vendor-live.test.mjs exercise exactly these directions.

F5 - 'check.mjs passes because it matched nothing.' Violation: both instruments print matched-input counts and the run refuses a green with a zero count on any axis. Measured: fleet operatorRefs=22 vehicleIds=14 chips=14 cells=108 labels=35 numbers=123 vendors=4 verbatim 11 of 11; police pvIds=10 camIds=18 cells=142 refusals=10 states=7 verbatim 16 of 16. Neither is zero.

F6 - 'The instrument cannot fail.' Violation: planted violations in both directions for both lenses: Fleet 6 of 6 caught, Police 17 of 17 caught, artboards restored byte-identically (4 and 2 hashes identical), baseline re-run green.
F7 - 'A merge is a ship.' Violation: both apps' serving revisions were read by field; the branch is on NEITHER; deploy_on_push is unset. Reported as needing a deploy, not as reached.
